entities.summary: Jean-Baptiste Budes, Comte de Guébriant was a French military leader who played a significant role in the Thirty Years War. Born in Saint-Carreuc, Brittany, in 1602, Budes joined the French army at the age of 20 and quickly rose through the ranks. By 1643, he had become the Marshal of France, serving under King Louis XIII. His military campaigns in Germany and the Netherlands earned him recognition and promotions. Budes died on November 24, 1643, at the age of 41, leaving behind a legacy as a skilled and courageous commander. He was the first of his family to hold the title of Marshal of France, paving the way for future generations. Budes' military achievements and leadership style were emulated by his contemporaries, and his name became synonymous with French military prowess. In the years following his death, Budes' exploits were immortalized in literature and art, cementing his place in French history. Despite his relatively short life, Budes' impact on the Thirty Years War and the French army was profound, and his legacy continues to be felt today.
